title: Nartatez vows impartiality after VP Sara slams PNP

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Sunday assured impartiality among its personnel after Vice President Sara Duterte earlier claimed that the organization has become "the enforcement arm of politicians."

“As an institution, we remain guided by the Constitution, the rule of law, and our commitment to serve all Filipinos fairly and impartially, with every action grounded in facts, evidence, and due process,” said PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. in a statement.

“Impartiality is a principle that we strive to uphold in every police operation and public service. Our commitment is to treat everyone with fairness, respect, and compassion, while providing equal protection under the law regardless of one's position or political affiliation,” he added.

The PNP responded to Duterte after the latter told Nartatez "to refrain from paying lip service to the claim that the organization is apolitical—a claim that virtually every Filipino knows to be untrue."
The police earlier said there was "no rescue or release" of a former household staff member of the Vice President and four other individuals.
The PNP pointed out that the concerned former staff members of Duterte were not being held captive when police accompanied their lawyers to a hotel in Taguig City on November 17.
In its latest statement, the PNP said that two legal counsels sought assistance from Fort Bonifacio Police Sub-Station 1 and requested police personnel to accompany them to the hotel.

It added that the five persons voluntarily went with police personnel to the police station. But they declined to execute affidavits regarding their alleged captivity and did not identify any person responsible for the supposed threats or coercion.

“The PNP remains ready to listen, receive complaints, and provide appropriate police assistance to anyone who feels threatened or unsafe. We will act on every report in accordance with established procedures," said Nartatez. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News
